analysis.investment_thesis: Anlon is a small-cap API/intermediates play with eye-popping profitability ratios (ROE 25.5%, ROCE 38.1%) and a seemingly attractive PEG (~0.63 on P/E 17.75 vs 28% revenue CAGR), but the reported earnings are not converting to cash — operating cash flow was negative in all 4 of the last 4 years, culminating in -23 Cr OCF on 21 Cr net profit in FY25. Until the cash-flow story matches the P&L story, this is a watch-list name, not a buy.
key_strengths: Strong returns on capital: ROE 25.5%, ROCE 38.1%, operating margin 33.7% expanding meaningfully (FY22 ~7% → FY25 26%).
Reasonable PEG: P/E 17.75 against 28% revenue CAGR and 97% op-income CAGR, with modest D/E of 0.27 post-equity raise.
Niche API/intermediates exporter across multiple therapeutic areas — the kind of small ~600 Cr Rajkot-based manufacturer that can scale into a multi-bagger if execution holds.
key_risks: Zero cash conversion: OCF negative 4/4 years, FY25 FCF -23 Cr — profits stuck in working capital or receivables.
Lumpy revenue (57→113→67→120) suggests customer/order concentration rather than steady compounding.
Recent equity infusion (equity 21→80 Cr) signals fresh IPO-era story stock with only 1 Cr cash and limited public track record.
red_flags: Net profit 21 Cr in FY25 but operating cash flow -23 Cr — a 44 Cr gap that needs explaining.
Revenue fell 41% in FY24 (113→67) before rebounding — growth is not linear.
FII holding just 0.32% and DII 4.6% — no institutional validation yet.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The headline numbers are the kind that normally make me pick up the phone: a tiny 616 Cr pharma-intermediates manufacturer in Rajkot, ROCE of 38%, operating margins expanding from single digits to 33.7%, and a PEG well under 1. On paper this looks like a classic Lynch "fast grower" in a niche I can understand — APIs for NSAIDs, antidepressants, GERD, diabetes — with India's CDMO/API tailwind still in early innings. The 3-year operating income CAGR of 97% against a P/E of just 17.75 is exactly the kind of mispricing I hunt for in the small-cap corner of the market.

But the story falls apart when I flip to the cash flow statement. Four straight years of negative operating cash flow, with the gap widening to -23 Cr in FY25 even as reported net profit hit 21 Cr, tells me the "earnings" are being funded by working capital build-up and fresh financing (19 Cr from financing activities, equity base ballooning from 21 to 80 Cr). The revenue line is also jagged — 113 Cr in FY23, then a collapse to 67 Cr in FY24 — which screams customer concentration or project-based lumpiness, not the steady market-share compounding I want. I'd want to see two consecutive years of positive OCF and a smoother revenue curve before paying up. Score 4, HOLD — put it on the watchlist, re-check at FY26 results.
